2609.26718.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
2609.26718.paper_summary: Long-context LLMs focus on retrieving distant evidence from extensive context, yet existing work has largely focused on overcoming distance alone. In this work, we identify the Proximity Trap, insufficient attention to distant evidence often arises less from distance itself than from cumulative competition with abundant, task-irrelevant proximal background. To address the Proximity Trap, we introduce LYRA (Long-context heavY-tailed Relevance Alignment), a t-distributed directional matching mechanism that reshapes the context retrieval distribution, directing more attention mass toward task-relevant evidence, while preserving the relative positional information encoded. Extensive experiments on LongBench-v2, RULER, and LongBench demonstrate consistent improvements across context lengths and task categories. We further introduce ProxBench, a multi-level fine-grained benchmark for evaluating distant evidence utilization under increasing proximal background interference. Project page: https://xiaoyuyoung.github.io/LYRA/
2609.26718.paper_summary_zh: 長期上下文的 LLM 專注於從廣泛的上下文中檢索遙遠的證據，但現有的研究在很大程度上僅專注於克服距離問題。在這項工作中，我們識別了「接近陷阱」，對遙遠證據的注意力不足往往不是由於距離本身，而是由於與大量與任務無關的近端背景的累積競爭。為了解決接近陷阱，我們引入了 LYRA（長期上下文重尾相關性對齊），這是一種 t 分佈的方向匹配機制，重塑上下文檢索分佈，將更多的注意力集中在與任務相關的證據上，同時保留編碼的相對位置信息。在 LongBench-v2、RULER 和 LongBench 上進行的廣泛實驗顯示，在上下文長度和任務類別上均有一致的改進。我們進一步引入了 ProxBench，一個多層次的細粒度基準，用於評估在增加的近端背景干擾下對遙遠證據的利用。項目頁面：https://xiaoyuyoung.github.io/LYRA/
